thesis: Mohnish Pabrai argues that philanthropy often lacks the rigorous input-to-output measurement and comparative analysis that capital allocators use in investing. He illustrates that unlike for-profit companies which face market-driven creative destruction if they fail to deliver value, many foundations can perpetually grow their endowments regardless of whether their charitable spending produces optimal social impact.
